scenes.heading: INT. HARPER HOUSE – KITCHEN – MORNING
scenes.text:
JAKE HARPER, 34, stands at the coffee maker.
Not unhappy.
Not happy.
A man who has gotten very good at occupying neutral
territory.
He pours two cups.
One black.
One with cream and two sugars.
He sets the second cup at the opposite side of the kitchen
island.
A practiced gesture.
An old kindness.
MAYA HARPER, 33, enters already dressed.
Professional even on weekends.
Phone in hand.
Work email open.
She is not cold.
She is tired.
2.
There is a difference.
Jake slides the coffee toward her.
JAKE
Cream. Two sugars.
Maya looks up.
Almost surprised.
MAYA
You remembered.
JAKE
Eventually, yeah.
A small smile.
It almost becomes something.
Then it dies.
The kind of smile that used to happen automatically.
Now requires effort.
Maya takes the coffee.
Checks her phone again.
Jake watches her for half a second too long.
She feels it.
MAYA
What?
JAKE
Nothing.
MAYA
That's never true.
Jake almost answers.
Doesn't.
Instead he looks out the kitchen window.
Avoidance as muscle memory.
Silence.
3.
Not hostile.
Worse.
Polite.
MAYA (CONT'D)
You grading today?
JAKE
Supposed to.
MAYA
Mm.
Another silence.
A marriage that has forgotten how to fight.
Jake stares at his coffee.
Then, abruptly:
JAKE
Let's go somewhere.
Maya doesn't look up.
MAYA
What?
JAKE
Today. Right now. Let's just get in
the car and drive.
She finally looks at him.
Trying to read whether this is spontaneity, panic, or a
delayed homework assignment from couples therapy.
MAYA
Drive where?
JAKE
I don't know.
MAYA
That is generally considered
important information.
JAKE
Anywhere.
Maya studies him.
4.
MAYA
Is this because of therapy?
JAKE
Maybe.
MAYA
Our therapist said "intentional
time.
" She did not say "randomly
disappear into rural Tennessee.
"
JAKE
I heard nuance.
MAYA
You heard the part where you didn't
have to plan.
JAKE
Also that.
For the first time all morning, she laughs.
A real laugh.
Tiny.
But real.
Jake notices.
The way a starving man notices food.
MAYA
You actually planned this?
JAKE
Five minutes ago.
MAYA
Which explains the confidence.
JAKE
Confidence is mostly just not
thinking things through.
Maya almost smiles again.
Then her eyes drop to the phone.
An email notification appears.
Jake sees it.
5.
The old version of him would have said something light.
The current version says nothing.
Maya locks the screen.
Sets the phone face down.
A decision.
Small, but not nothing.
MAYA
Fine.
Jake blinks.
JAKE
Seriously?
MAYA
Before I change my mind.
Jake smiles.
A genuine one.
The first we've seen.

scenes.heading: INT. SUV – MOVING – DAY
scenes.text:
Jake drives.
Maya watches the scenery pass.
For a while, they simply exist together.
Comfortably.
Like they used to.
6.
Music plays low.
Not their song.
Just something old enough to feel shared.
MAYA
Remember Gatlinburg?
JAKE
Which disaster?
MAYA
The cabin.
JAKE
Oh God.
MAYA
The bear.
JAKE
That bear broke into our honeymoon.
MAYA
Technically, you left the cooler
outside.
JAKE
The bear was a criminal.
MAYA
The bear was hungry.
JAKE
The bear stole my hamburgers.
MAYA
The bear stole your hamburgers
because you challenged nature.
Jake laughs.
Maya laughs.
For a moment they are themselves again.
Then the laughter thins.
Silence settles.
Not painful at first.
Then, slowly, painful.
7.
Maya looks out the window.
JAKE
What?
MAYA
Nothing.
JAKE
Again, statistically never true.
Maya hesitates.
MAYA
I just forgot what this felt like.
Jake knows exactly what she means.
The silence after that says everything.
He looks ahead.
Keeps driving.
Avoiding the thing that would need to be said next.
Maya lets him.
For now.
A beat.
MAYA (CONT'D)
You ever notice how everybody wants
to be understood?
Jake glances over.
JAKE
That's a turn.
MAYA
I'm serious.
JAKE
I could tell by the sudden
emotional danger.
Maya smiles faintly.
Then:
8.
MAYA
Everybody says they want someone to
really see them. Really know them.
JAKE
Okay.
MAYA
But the second somebody does...
they panic.
Jake keeps his eyes on the road.
JAKE
You talking generally?
MAYA
Maybe.
JAKE
That's ominous.
MAYA
It's true.
Jake says nothing.
Maya watches him.
MAYA (CONT'D)
You know, silence is also an
answer.
JAKE
I was hoping it was more of a
pause.
MAYA
You use a lot of pauses.
JAKE
They're affordable.
She gives him a look.
Not cruel.
Accurate.
MAYA
Jake.
He tightens his grip on the wheel.
9.
Just slightly.
JAKE
I'm trying.
MAYA
I know.
And that somehow hurts more than accusation.

scenes.heading: INT. SUV – MOVING – CONTINUOUS
scenes.text:
Maya watches the woods.
MAYA
This doesn't feel like a
turnaround.
JAKE
It's a road. Roads go places.
MAYA
Inspirational.
JAKE
Thank you.
Maya looks at the dash clock.
The numbers flicker.
Just once.
She notices.
Jake doesn't.
MAYA
Did you see that?
JAKE
See what?
The clock is normal again.
Maya looks out at the trees.
Something about this place feels isolated in a way she can't
explain.
Which bothers her.
She is an engineer.
13.
Explanation is how she survives.
Ahead —
the trees suddenly break.
The road opens into a wide clearing.
Jake slows instinctively.
MAYA
Jake...
The clearing stretches perhaps two hundred yards across.
Several vehicles.
Men.
Equipment.
Crates.
Portable floodlights mounted on towers.
Not construction.
Not logging.
Not military.
Not anything immediately recognizable.
Jake brings the SUV nearly to a stop.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Keep driving.
JAKE
Yeah.
But neither of them can stop looking.
Something is happening.
A transaction.
Groups moving methodically between vehicles.
Large black cases being transferred.
Nobody speaking loudly.
Nobody wasting movement.
14.
The atmosphere feels formal.
Professional.
Organized.
And wrong.
Maya leans forward.
MAYA
What is that?
Jake squints.
Near the center of the clearing sits a large matte-black
vehicle.
Its shape is difficult to process.
Angular.
Geometric.
Not futuristic.
Not sleek.
Simply incorrect.
Like the designer solved different problems than human
machines are built to solve.
The proportions bother Maya immediately.
Her eyes move across it.
Roofline.
Wheel placement.
Load bearing.
Angles.
Every instinct she possesses starts quietly screaming.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Stop.
Jake stops.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Something's wrong.
15.
JAKE
You got all that from a parked car?
MAYA
Look at it.
JAKE
I'm looking.
MAYA
No. Actually look.
Jake studies it.
At first he sees nothing.
Then —
something.
The roofline.
The wheel placement.
The way the body seems balanced around a center of gravity
that should not exist.
JAKE
Why does it feel weird?
MAYA
I don't know.
The answer bothers her.
She always knows.
MAYA (CONT'D)
The geometry doesn't work.
JAKE
Geometry?
MAYA
The weight distribution should be
impossible.
Jake looks again.
Now he sees it too.
The vehicle somehow appears balanced incorrectly.
As though gravity itself behaves differently inside it.
16.
Nearby —
a large crate opens.
Several men remove objects from protective foam.
Weapons.
At least they resemble weapons.
Long.
Black.
Mechanical.
Except the grips are wrong.
The trigger spacing is wrong.
The proportions are wrong.
Designed for hands that aren't quite human.
Silence.
Jake and Maya stare.
Neither breathing.
JAKE
Maya.
MAYA
I know.
JAKE
Tell me I'm imagining that.
MAYA
I can't.
Jake slowly shifts the SUV into reverse.
Careful.
Quiet.
Nobody has noticed them.
Not yet.
The SUV begins backing away.
17.
Ten feet.
Twenty.
Thirty.
Maya never takes her eyes off the clearing.
Then something else catches her attention.
The people.
Not all of them are people.
At least —
not exactly.
Several figures stand near the matte-black vehicles.
Tall.
Very tall.
Wearing dark clothing.
Motionless.
Too symmetrical.
Too patient.
The air around them seems oddly still.
Rain-dark clouds move overhead, but their clothing does not
stir.
Maya feels cold.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Jake.
JAKE
Don't.
MAYA
There are people standing by those
vehicles.
JAKE
Don't say aliens.
MAYA
I wasn't going to.
18.
Beat.
MAYA (CONT'D)
But now I'm thinking it.
The SUV continues reversing.
Almost clear.
Almost gone.
Then —
CRACK.
A branch snaps beneath the rear tire.
Loud.
Violently loud.
The sound echoes through the clearing.
Everything stops.
Every movement.
Every conversation.
Every transfer.
Twenty heads turn.
All at once.
Toward the SUV.
Toward Jake and Maya.
Silence.
Absolute silence.
Nobody shouts.
Nobody points.
Nobody runs.
That stillness is somehow worse.
Jake stares.
The people stare back.
19.
Then one of the tall figures slowly tilts its head.
Studying them.
Not surprised.
Interested.
Inside the SUV, the radio crackles.
Static.
Not from any station.
A low, almost subsonic tone slips underneath it.
Maya whispers:
MAYA (CONT'D)
Go.
Jake doesn't move.
Frozen.
The figure continues watching.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Jake.
Nothing.
MAYA (CONT'D)
JAKE. GO.
The spell breaks.
Jake slams the accelerator.
The SUV fishtails.
Dirt sprays.
The vehicle rockets backward down the road.
Inside —
pure panic.
JAKE
What the hell was that?
MAYA
I don't know!
20.
JAKE
What did we just see?
MAYA
I DON'T KNOW!
Behind them —
nothing.
No pursuit.
No headlights.
No engines.
Just forest.
Jake races through the trees.
Heart pounding.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Maybe it's military.
JAKE
Military doesn't build cars like
that.
MAYA
Maybe experimental.
JAKE
Experimental for who?
MAYA
I don't know!
The road twists.
The SUV nearly slides off the shoulder.
Jake corrects.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Slow down!
JAKE
No!
Then —
through the rear window —
21.
headlights.
Far behind.
Emerging from the trees.
One pair.
Then another.
Then another.
Black SUVs.
Fast.
Professional.
Closing.
Maya sees them first.
Her face drains of color.
MAYA
Jake.
JAKE
What?
MAYA
They're coming.
Jake looks.
His stomach drops.
Three black SUVs.
Moving with terrifying precision.
Not reckless.
Not desperate.
Certain.
As though they already know exactly how this ends.
JAKE
Oh God.
22.
The chase begins.

scene_001.heading: EXT. SUBURBAN TENNESSEE STREET – MORNING
scene_001.text:
A quiet Saturday.
Birds.
Sprinklers ticking across lawns.
A distant mower chewing through somebody's idea of peace.
Ordinary America.
The kind of morning that makes crisis feel impossible.

scene_002.heading: INT. HARPER HOUSE – KITCHEN – MORNING
scene_002.text:
JAKE HARPER, 34, stands at the coffee maker.
Not unhappy.
Not happy.
A man who has gotten very good at occupying neutral
territory.
He pours two cups.
One black.
One with cream and two sugars.
He sets the second cup at the opposite side of the kitchen
island.
A practiced gesture.
An old kindness.
MAYA HARPER, 33, enters already dressed.
Professional even on weekends.
Phone in hand.
Work email open.
She is not cold.
She is tired.
2.
There is a difference.
Jake slides the coffee toward her.
JAKE
Cream. Two sugars.
Maya looks up.
Almost surprised.
MAYA
You remembered.
JAKE
Eventually, yeah.
A small smile.
It almost becomes something.
Then it dies.
The kind of smile that used to happen automatically.
Now requires effort.
Maya takes the coffee.
Checks her phone again.
Jake watches her for half a second too long.
She feels it.
MAYA
What?
JAKE
Nothing.
MAYA
That's never true.
Jake almost answers.
Doesn't.
Instead he looks out the kitchen window.
Avoidance as muscle memory.
Silence.
3.
Not hostile.
Worse.
Polite.
MAYA (CONT'D)
You grading today?
JAKE
Supposed to.
MAYA
Mm.
Another silence.
A marriage that has forgotten how to fight.
Jake stares at his coffee.
Then, abruptly:
JAKE
Let's go somewhere.
Maya doesn't look up.
MAYA
What?
JAKE
Today. Right now. Let's just get in
the car and drive.
She finally looks at him.
Trying to read whether this is spontaneity, panic, or a
delayed homework assignment from couples therapy.
MAYA
Drive where?
JAKE
I don't know.
MAYA
That is generally considered
important information.
JAKE
Anywhere.
Maya studies him.
4.
MAYA
Is this because of therapy?
JAKE
Maybe.
MAYA
Our therapist said "intentional
time.
" She did not say "randomly
disappear into rural Tennessee.
"
JAKE
I heard nuance.
MAYA
You heard the part where you didn't
have to plan.
JAKE
Also that.
For the first time all morning, she laughs.
A real laugh.
Tiny.
But real.
Jake notices.
The way a starving man notices food.
MAYA
You actually planned this?
JAKE
Five minutes ago.
MAYA
Which explains the confidence.
JAKE
Confidence is mostly just not
thinking things through.
Maya almost smiles again.
Then her eyes drop to the phone.
An email notification appears.
Jake sees it.
5.
The old version of him would have said something light.
The current version says nothing.
Maya locks the screen.
Sets the phone face down.
A decision.
Small, but not nothing.
MAYA
Fine.
Jake blinks.
JAKE
Seriously?
MAYA
Before I change my mind.
Jake smiles.
A genuine one.
The first we've seen.
CUT TO:

scene_003.heading: EXT. HIGHWAY – LATER
scene_003.text:
Their SUV moves through rolling Tennessee countryside.
Green hills.
Two-lane roads.
Late morning light sliding across the windshield.

scene_004.heading: INT. SUV – MOVING – DAY
scene_004.text:
Jake drives.
Maya watches the scenery pass.
For a while, they simply exist together.
Comfortably.
Like they used to.
6.
Music plays low.
Not their song.
Just something old enough to feel shared.
MAYA
Remember Gatlinburg?
JAKE
Which disaster?
MAYA
The cabin.
JAKE
Oh God.
MAYA
The bear.
JAKE
That bear broke into our honeymoon.
MAYA
Technically, you left the cooler
outside.
JAKE
The bear was a criminal.
MAYA
The bear was hungry.
JAKE
The bear stole my hamburgers.
MAYA
The bear stole your hamburgers
because you challenged nature.
Jake laughs.
Maya laughs.
For a moment they are themselves again.
Then the laughter thins.
Silence settles.
Not painful at first.
Then, slowly, painful.
7.
Maya looks out the window.
JAKE
What?
MAYA
Nothing.
JAKE
Again, statistically never true.
Maya hesitates.
MAYA
I just forgot what this felt like.
Jake knows exactly what she means.
The silence after that says everything.
He looks ahead.
Keeps driving.
Avoiding the thing that would need to be said next.
Maya lets him.
For now.
A beat.
MAYA (CONT'D)
You ever notice how everybody wants
to be understood?
Jake glances over.
JAKE
That's a turn.
MAYA
I'm serious.
JAKE
I could tell by the sudden
emotional danger.
Maya smiles faintly.
Then:
8.
MAYA
Everybody says they want someone to
really see them. Really know them.
JAKE
Okay.
MAYA
But the second somebody does...
they panic.
Jake keeps his eyes on the road.
JAKE
You talking generally?
MAYA
Maybe.
JAKE
That's ominous.
MAYA
It's true.
Jake says nothing.
Maya watches him.
MAYA (CONT'D)
You know, silence is also an
answer.
JAKE
I was hoping it was more of a
pause.
MAYA
You use a lot of pauses.
JAKE
They're affordable.
She gives him a look.
Not cruel.
Accurate.
MAYA
Jake.
He tightens his grip on the wheel.
9.
Just slightly.
JAKE
I'm trying.
MAYA
I know.
And that somehow hurts more than accusation.

scene_005.heading: EXT. BACK ROAD – AFTERNOON
scene_005.text:
The highway gives way to smaller roads.
Then smaller roads.
Then roads that seem less maintained than remembered.
The sky slowly changes color.
The day getting away from them.

scene_006.heading: INT. SUV – MOVING – AFTERNOON
scene_006.text:
Maya glances at her phone.
One percent.
MAYA
You know we're lost.
JAKE
We're exploring.
MAYA
Lost people always rename it.
The phone dies.
Black screen.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Fantastic.
JAKE
We've got road signs.
MAYA
You've ignored three.
JAKE
They looked judgmental.
10.
She shakes her head.
But she's smiling.
Then she notices something ahead.
Or rather behind.
MAYA
Jake.
JAKE
Yeah?
MAYA
You missed the turn.
Jake looks.
The turn is already disappearing in the rearview mirror.
JAKE
Damn.
MAYA
You always do that.
JAKE
Do what?
MAYA
Decide you're right before
checking.
The smile disappears.
The old argument arriving.
JAKE
We're talking about a road.
MAYA
We're never talking about the road.
Silence.
Jake grips the wheel.
There it is.
The thing beneath the thing.
He could answer.
11.
He could turn toward it.
Instead, he looks ahead.
Outside the windshield —
A narrow, unmarked road disappears into dense forest.
JAKE
I'll turn around.
MAYA
There?
JAKE
Looks wide enough.
MAYA
Jake—
But he's already turning.
The SUV leaves the paved road.
The trees swallow them.
And for the first time in the film —
something feels wrong.
Not dramatic.
Not supernatural.
Just the faint sensation that the world has stopped being
casual.
CUT TO BLACK.
TITLE: THE SCENIC ROUTE
FADE IN FROM BLACK:

scene_007.heading: EXT. FOREST ROAD – LATE AFTERNOON
scene_007.text:
The SUV crawls down the narrow dirt road.
Trees crowd both sides.
The canopy overhead thick enough to dim the sunlight.
No houses.
12.
No fences.
No signs.
No power lines.
No tire ruts except their own.
Even the birds have gone quiet.

scene_008.heading: INT. SUV – MOVING – CONTINUOUS
scene_008.text:
Maya watches the woods.
MAYA
This doesn't feel like a
turnaround.
JAKE
It's a road. Roads go places.
MAYA
Inspirational.
JAKE
Thank you.
Maya looks at the dash clock.
The numbers flicker.
Just once.
She notices.
Jake doesn't.
MAYA
Did you see that?
JAKE
See what?
The clock is normal again.
Maya looks out at the trees.
Something about this place feels isolated in a way she can't
explain.
Which bothers her.
She is an engineer.
13.
Explanation is how she survives.
Ahead —
the trees suddenly break.
The road opens into a wide clearing.
Jake slows instinctively.
MAYA
Jake...
The clearing stretches perhaps two hundred yards across.
Several vehicles.
Men.
Equipment.
Crates.
Portable floodlights mounted on towers.
Not construction.
Not logging.
Not military.
Not anything immediately recognizable.
Jake brings the SUV nearly to a stop.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Keep driving.
JAKE
Yeah.
But neither of them can stop looking.
Something is happening.
A transaction.
Groups moving methodically between vehicles.
Large black cases being transferred.
Nobody speaking loudly.
Nobody wasting movement.
14.
The atmosphere feels formal.
Professional.
Organized.
And wrong.
Maya leans forward.
MAYA
What is that?
Jake squints.
Near the center of the clearing sits a large matte-black
vehicle.
Its shape is difficult to process.
Angular.
Geometric.
Not futuristic.
Not sleek.
Simply incorrect.
Like the designer solved different problems than human
machines are built to solve.
The proportions bother Maya immediately.
Her eyes move across it.
Roofline.
Wheel placement.
Load bearing.
Angles.
Every instinct she possesses starts quietly screaming.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Stop.
Jake stops.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Something's wrong.
15.
JAKE
You got all that from a parked car?
MAYA
Look at it.
JAKE
I'm looking.
MAYA
No. Actually look.
Jake studies it.
At first he sees nothing.
Then —
something.
The roofline.
The wheel placement.
The way the body seems balanced around a center of gravity
that should not exist.
JAKE
Why does it feel weird?
MAYA
I don't know.
The answer bothers her.
She always knows.
MAYA (CONT'D)
The geometry doesn't work.
JAKE
Geometry?
MAYA
The weight distribution should be
impossible.
Jake looks again.
Now he sees it too.
The vehicle somehow appears balanced incorrectly.
As though gravity itself behaves differently inside it.
16.
Nearby —
a large crate opens.
Several men remove objects from protective foam.
Weapons.
At least they resemble weapons.
Long.
Black.
Mechanical.
Except the grips are wrong.
The trigger spacing is wrong.
The proportions are wrong.
Designed for hands that aren't quite human.
Silence.
Jake and Maya stare.
Neither breathing.
JAKE
Maya.
MAYA
I know.
JAKE
Tell me I'm imagining that.
MAYA
I can't.
Jake slowly shifts the SUV into reverse.
Careful.
Quiet.
Nobody has noticed them.
Not yet.
The SUV begins backing away.
17.
Ten feet.
Twenty.
Thirty.
Maya never takes her eyes off the clearing.
Then something else catches her attention.
The people.
Not all of them are people.
At least —
not exactly.
Several figures stand near the matte-black vehicles.
Tall.
Very tall.
Wearing dark clothing.
Motionless.
Too symmetrical.
Too patient.
The air around them seems oddly still.
Rain-dark clouds move overhead, but their clothing does not
stir.
Maya feels cold.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Jake.
JAKE
Don't.
MAYA
There are people standing by those
vehicles.
JAKE
Don't say aliens.
MAYA
I wasn't going to.
18.
Beat.
MAYA (CONT'D)
But now I'm thinking it.
The SUV continues reversing.
Almost clear.
Almost gone.
Then —
CRACK.
A branch snaps beneath the rear tire.
Loud.
Violently loud.
The sound echoes through the clearing.
Everything stops.
Every movement.
Every conversation.
Every transfer.
Twenty heads turn.
All at once.
Toward the SUV.
Toward Jake and Maya.
Silence.
Absolute silence.
Nobody shouts.
Nobody points.
Nobody runs.
That stillness is somehow worse.
Jake stares.
The people stare back.
19.
Then one of the tall figures slowly tilts its head.
Studying them.
Not surprised.
Interested.
Inside the SUV, the radio crackles.
Static.
Not from any station.
A low, almost subsonic tone slips underneath it.
Maya whispers:
MAYA (CONT'D)
Go.
Jake doesn't move.
Frozen.
The figure continues watching.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Jake.
Nothing.
MAYA (CONT'D)
JAKE. GO.
The spell breaks.
Jake slams the accelerator.
The SUV fishtails.
Dirt sprays.
The vehicle rockets backward down the road.
Inside —
pure panic.
JAKE
What the hell was that?
MAYA
I don't know!
20.
JAKE
What did we just see?
MAYA
I DON'T KNOW!
Behind them —
nothing.
No pursuit.
No headlights.
No engines.
Just forest.
Jake races through the trees.
Heart pounding.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Maybe it's military.
JAKE
Military doesn't build cars like
that.
MAYA
Maybe experimental.
JAKE
Experimental for who?
MAYA
I don't know!
The road twists.
The SUV nearly slides off the shoulder.
Jake corrects.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Slow down!
JAKE
No!
Then —
through the rear window —
21.
headlights.
Far behind.
Emerging from the trees.
One pair.
Then another.
Then another.
Black SUVs.
Fast.
Professional.
Closing.
Maya sees them first.
Her face drains of color.
MAYA
Jake.
JAKE
What?
MAYA
They're coming.
Jake looks.
His stomach drops.
Three black SUVs.
Moving with terrifying precision.
Not reckless.
Not desperate.
Certain.
As though they already know exactly how this ends.
JAKE
Oh God.
22.
The chase begins.
SMASH CUT TO:

scene_009.heading: EXT. TENNESSEE HIGHWAY – CONTINUOUS
scene_009.text:
The SUV bursts from the forest road onto open highway.
Jake jerks the wheel.
Traffic swerves.
Horns.
The vehicle straightens.
The black SUVs emerge seconds later.
Then something unexpected happens.
They slow down.
No attempt to ram them.
No attempt to pass.
No attempt to stop them.
They simply fall back.
Watching.
Following.
Maya notices immediately.
And that scares her even more.
MAYA
Why aren't they stopping us?
Jake doesn't answer.
Because he already knows.
People who aren't worried about losing you are the most
dangerous people in the world.
CUT TO:
23.

scene_010.heading: EXT. HIGHWAY GAS STATION – EVENING
scene_010.text:
The station sits alone beside the road.
Four pumps.
One service bay.
A flickering OPEN sign fighting a losing battle against age.
The kind of place travelers forget five minutes after
leaving.
Jake pulls in hard.
The SUV skids slightly.
Stops beside a pump.
For a second neither moves.
Both breathing hard.
Trying to process what just happened.

previs_scene_board.intent:
A quiet Saturday.
Birds.
Sprinklers ticking across lawns.
A distant mower chewing through somebody's idea of peace.
Ordinary America.
The kind of morning that makes crisis feel impossible.

JAKE HARPER, 34, stands at the coffee maker.
Not unhappy.
Not happy.
A man who has gotten very good at occupying neutral
territory.
He pours two cups.
One black.
One with cream and two sugars.
He sets the second cup at the opposite side of the kitchen
island.
A practiced gesture.
An old kindness.
MAYA HARPER, 33, enters already dressed.
Professional even on weekends.
Phone in hand.
Work email open.
She is not cold.
She is tired.
2.
There is a difference.
Jake slides the coffee toward her.
JAKE
Cream. Two sugars.
Maya looks up.
Almost surprised.
MAYA
You remembered.
JAKE
Eventually, yeah.
A small smile.
It almost becomes something.
Then it dies.
The kind of smile that used to happen automatically.
Now requires effort.
Maya takes the coffee.
Checks her phone again.
Jake watches her for half a second too long.
She feels it.
MAYA
What?
JAKE
Nothing.
MAYA
That's never true.
Jake almost answers.
Doesn't.
Instead he looks out the kitchen window.
Avoidance as muscle memory.
Silence.
3.
Not hostile.
Worse.
Polite.
MAYA (CONT'D)
You grading today?
JAKE
Supposed to.
MAYA
Mm.
Another silence.
A marriage that has forgotten how to fight.
Jake stares at his coffee.
Then, abruptly:
JAKE
Let's go somewhere.
Maya doesn't look up.
MAYA
What?
JAKE
Today. Right now. Let's just get in
the car and drive.
She finally looks at him.
Trying to read whether this is spontaneity, panic, or a
delayed homework assignment from couples therapy.
MAYA
Drive where?
JAKE
I don't know.
MAYA
That is generally considered
important information.
JAKE
Anywhere.
Maya studies him.
4.
MAYA
Is this because of therapy?
JAKE
Maybe.
MAYA
Our therapist said "intentional
time.
" She did not say "randomly
disappear into rural Tennessee.
"
JAKE
I heard nuance.
MAYA
You heard the part where you didn't
have to plan.
JAKE
Also that.
For the first time all morning, she laughs.
A real laugh.
Tiny.
But real.
Jake notices.
The way a starving man notices food.
MAYA
You actually planned this?
JAKE
Five minutes ago.
MAYA
Which explains the confidence.
JAKE
Confidence is mostly just not
thinking things through.
Maya almost smiles again.
Then her eyes drop to the phone.
An email notification appears.
Jake sees it.
5.
The old version of him would have said something light.
The current version says nothing.
Maya locks the screen.
Sets the phone face down.
A decision.
Small, but not nothing.
MAYA
Fine.
Jake blinks.
JAKE
Seriously?
MAYA
Before I change my mind.
Jake smiles.
A genuine one.
The first we've seen.
CUT TO:

Their SUV moves through rolling Tennessee countryside.
Green hills.
Two-lane roads.
Late morning light sliding across the windshield.

Jake drives.
Maya watches the scenery pass.
For a while, they simply exist together.
Comfortably.
Like they used to.
6.
Music plays low.
Not their song.
Just something old enough to feel shared.
MAYA
Remember Gatlinburg?
JAKE
Which disaster?
MAYA
The cabin.
JAKE
Oh God.
MAYA
The bear.
JAKE
That bear broke into our honeymoon.
MAYA
Technically, you left the cooler
outside.
JAKE
The bear was a criminal.
MAYA
The bear was hungry.
JAKE
The bear stole my hamburgers.
MAYA
The bear stole your hamburgers
because you challenged nature.
Jake laughs.
Maya laughs.
For a moment they are themselves again.
Then the laughter thins.
Silence settles.
Not painful at first.
Then, slowly, painful.
7.
Maya looks out the window.
JAKE
What?
MAYA
Nothing.
JAKE
Again, statistically never true.
Maya hesitates.
MAYA
I just forgot what this felt like.
Jake knows exactly what she means.
The silence after that says everything.
He looks ahead.
Keeps driving.
Avoiding the thing that would need to be said next.
Maya lets him.
For now.
A beat.
MAYA (CONT'D)
You ever notice how everybody wants
to be understood?
Jake glances over.
JAKE
That's a turn.
MAYA
I'm serious.
JAKE
I could tell by the sudden
emotional danger.
Maya smiles faintly.
Then:
8.
MAYA
Everybody says they want someone to
really see them. Really know them.
JAKE
Okay.
MAYA
But the second somebody does...
they panic.
Jake keeps his eyes on the road.
JAKE
You talking generally?
MAYA
Maybe.
JAKE
That's ominous.
MAYA
It's true.
Jake says nothing.
Maya watches him.
MAYA (CONT'D)
You know, silence is also an
answer.
JAKE
I was hoping it was more of a
pause.
MAYA
You use a lot of pauses.
JAKE
They're affordable.
She gives him a look.
Not cruel.
Accurate.
MAYA
Jake.
He tightens his grip on the wheel.
9.
Just slightly.
JAKE
I'm trying.
MAYA
I know.
And that somehow hurts more than accusation.

The highway gives way to smaller roads.
Then smaller roads.
Then roads that seem less maintained than remembered.
The sky slowly changes color.
The day getting away from them.

Maya glances at her phone.
One percent.
MAYA
You know we're lost.
JAKE
We're exploring.
MAYA
Lost people always rename it.
The phone dies.
Black screen.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Fantastic.
JAKE
We've got road signs.
MAYA
You've ignored three.
JAKE
They looked judgmental.
10.
She shakes her head.
But she's smiling.
Then she notices something ahead.
Or rather behind.
MAYA
Jake.
JAKE
Yeah?
MAYA
You missed the turn.
Jake looks.
The turn is already disappearing in the rearview mirror.
JAKE
Damn.
MAYA
You always do that.
JAKE
Do what?
MAYA
Decide you're right before
checking.
The smile disappears.
The old argument arriving.
JAKE
We're talking about a road.
MAYA
We're never talking about the road.
Silence.
Jake grips the wheel.
There it is.
The thing beneath the thing.
He could answer.
11.
He could turn toward it.
Instead, he looks ahead.
Outside the windshield —
A narrow, unmarked road disappears into dense forest.
JAKE
I'll turn around.
MAYA
There?
JAKE
Looks wide enough.
MAYA
Jake—
But he's already turning.
The SUV leaves the paved road.
The trees swallow them.
And for the first time in the film —
something feels wrong.
Not dramatic.
Not supernatural.
Just the faint sensation that the world has stopped being
casual.
CUT TO BLACK.
TITLE: THE SCENIC ROUTE
FADE IN FROM BLACK:

The SUV crawls down the narrow dirt road.
Trees crowd both sides.
The canopy overhead thick enough to dim the sunlight.
No houses.
12.
No fences.
No signs.
No power lines.
No tire ruts except their own.
Even the birds have gone quiet.

Maya watches the woods.
MAYA
This doesn't feel like a
turnaround.
JAKE
It's a road. Roads go places.
MAYA
Inspirational.
JAKE
Thank you.
Maya looks at the dash clock.
The numbers flicker.
Just once.
She notices.
Jake doesn't.
MAYA
Did you see that?
JAKE
See what?
The clock is normal again.
Maya looks out at the trees.
Something about this place feels isolated in a way she can't
explain.
Which bothers her.
She is an engineer.
13.
Explanation is how she survives.
Ahead —
the trees suddenly break.
The road opens into a wide clearing.
Jake slows instinctively.
MAYA
Jake...
The clearing stretches perhaps two hundred yards across.
Several vehicles.
Men.
Equipment.
Crates.
Portable floodlights mounted on towers.
Not construction.
Not logging.
Not military.
Not anything immediately recognizable.
Jake brings the SUV nearly to a stop.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Keep driving.
JAKE
Yeah.
But neither of them can stop looking.
Something is happening.
A transaction.
Groups moving methodically between vehicles.
Large black cases being transferred.
Nobody speaking loudly.
Nobody wasting movement.
14.
The atmosphere feels formal.
Professional.
Organized.
And wrong.
Maya leans forward.
MAYA
What is that?
Jake squints.
Near the center of the clearing sits a large matte-black
vehicle.
Its shape is difficult to process.
Angular.
Geometric.
Not futuristic.
Not sleek.
Simply incorrect.
Like the designer solved different problems than human
machines are built to solve.
The proportions bother Maya immediately.
Her eyes move across it.
Roofline.
Wheel placement.
Load bearing.
Angles.
Every instinct she possesses starts quietly screaming.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Stop.
Jake stops.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Something's wrong.
15.
JAKE
You got all that from a parked car?
MAYA
Look at it.
JAKE
I'm looking.
MAYA
No. Actually look.
Jake studies it.
At first he sees nothing.
Then —
something.
The roofline.
The wheel placement.
The way the body seems balanced around a center of gravity
that should not exist.
JAKE
Why does it feel weird?
MAYA
I don't know.
The answer bothers her.
She always knows.
MAYA (CONT'D)
The geometry doesn't work.
JAKE
Geometry?
MAYA
The weight distribution should be
impossible.
Jake looks again.
Now he sees it too.
The vehicle somehow appears balanced incorrectly.
As though gravity itself behaves differently inside it.
16.
Nearby —
a large crate opens.
Several men remove objects from protective foam.
Weapons.
At least they resemble weapons.
Long.
Black.
Mechanical.
Except the grips are wrong.
The trigger spacing is wrong.
The proportions are wrong.
Designed for hands that aren't quite human.
Silence.
Jake and Maya stare.
Neither breathing.
JAKE
Maya.
MAYA
I know.
JAKE
Tell me I'm imagining that.
MAYA
I can't.
Jake slowly shifts the SUV into reverse.
Careful.
Quiet.
Nobody has noticed them.
Not yet.
The SUV begins backing away.
17.
Ten feet.
Twenty.
Thirty.
Maya never takes her eyes off the clearing.
Then something else catches her attention.
The people.
Not all of them are people.
At least —
not exactly.
Several figures stand near the matte-black vehicles.
Tall.
Very tall.
Wearing dark clothing.
Motionless.
Too symmetrical.
Too patient.
The air around them seems oddly still.
Rain-dark clouds move overhead, but their clothing does not
stir.
Maya feels cold.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Jake.
JAKE
Don't.
MAYA
There are people standing by those
vehicles.
JAKE
Don't say aliens.
MAYA
I wasn't going to.
18.
Beat.
MAYA (CONT'D)
But now I'm thinking it.
The SUV continues reversing.
Almost clear.
Almost gone.
Then —
CRACK.
A branch snaps beneath the rear tire.
Loud.
Violently loud.
The sound echoes through the clearing.
Everything stops.
Every movement.
Every conversation.
Every transfer.
Twenty heads turn.
All at once.
Toward the SUV.
Toward Jake and Maya.
Silence.
Absolute silence.
Nobody shouts.
Nobody points.
Nobody runs.
That stillness is somehow worse.
Jake stares.
The people stare back.
19.
Then one of the tall figures slowly tilts its head.
Studying them.
Not surprised.
Interested.
Inside the SUV, the radio crackles.
Static.
Not from any station.
A low, almost subsonic tone slips underneath it.
Maya whispers:
MAYA (CONT'D)
Go.
Jake doesn't move.
Frozen.
The figure continues watching.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Jake.
Nothing.
MAYA (CONT'D)
JAKE. GO.
The spell breaks.
Jake slams the accelerator.
The SUV fishtails.
Dirt sprays.
The vehicle rockets backward down the road.
Inside —
pure panic.
JAKE
What the hell was that?
MAYA
I don't know!
20.
JAKE
What did we just see?
MAYA
I DON'T KNOW!
Behind them —
nothing.
No pursuit.
No headlights.
No engines.
Just forest.
Jake races through the trees.
Heart pounding.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Maybe it's military.
JAKE
Military doesn't build cars like
that.
MAYA
Maybe experimental.
JAKE
Experimental for who?
MAYA
I don't know!
The road twists.
The SUV nearly slides off the shoulder.
Jake corrects.
MAYA (CONT'D)
Slow down!
JAKE
No!
Then —
through the rear window —
21.
headlights.
Far behind.
Emerging from the trees.
One pair.
Then another.
Then another.
Black SUVs.
Fast.
Professional.
Closing.
Maya sees them first.
Her face drains of color.
MAYA
Jake.
JAKE
What?
MAYA
They're coming.
Jake looks.
His stomach drops.
Three black SUVs.
Moving with terrifying precision.
Not reckless.
Not desperate.
Certain.
As though they already know exactly how this ends.
JAKE
Oh God.
22.
The chase begins.
SMASH CUT TO:

The SUV bursts from the forest road onto open highway.
Jake jerks the wheel.
Traffic swerves.
Horns.
The vehicle straightens.
The black SUVs emerge seconds later.
Then something unexpected happens.
They slow down.
No attempt to ram them.
No attempt to pass.
No attempt to stop them.
They simply fall back.
Watching.
Following.
Maya notices immediately.
And that scares her even more.
MAYA
Why aren't they stopping us?
Jake doesn't answer.
Because he already knows.
People who aren't worried about losing you are the most
dangerous people in the world.
CUT TO:
23.

The station sits alone beside the road.
Four pumps.
One service bay.
A flickering OPEN sign fighting a losing battle against age.
The kind of place travelers forget five minutes after
leaving.
Jake pulls in hard.
The SUV skids slightly.
Stops beside a pump.
For a second neither moves.
Both breathing hard.
Trying to process what just happened.
